```{r Workshop 2}
#2.16 Load packages
#install.packages("tidyverse")
#library(tidyverse)
mpg
?mpg
#2.17 Create your first ggplot
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))
#2.18 Understanding the grammar of graphics
#2.18.1 graphing template
#ggplot(data = <DATA>) +
  #<GEOM_FUCTION>(mapping = aes(<MAPPINGS))
#2.18.2 Aesthetic mappings
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class)) #colour
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, size = class)) #size
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, alpha = class)) #alpha
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, shape = class)) #shape
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), colour = "blue") #remember to change ()
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), colour = displ < 5) # it cant find it 
#2.19 Troubleshooting 
ggplot(data=mpg)
+  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), colour = "blue") # + should be on the top line
#2.20 Facet and panel plots
#facet_wrap() only use for discrete variables
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  facet_wrap (~ class, nrow= 2)
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  facet_grid(drv ~ cyl) #more than one variable
?facet_wrap
#very good for publication 
#2.21 Fitting simple lines
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) #display data as points
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) #display as smooth lines
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, linetype = drv)) #change the line type
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, group = drv)) #allows you to group
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = drv), show.legend = FALSE) #change the colour of each line based on drv value
ggplot(data=mpg) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_smooth(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) #plot multiple geoms
ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() #same plot as above but more efficient
ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(colour = class)) +
  geom_smooth() #style points by themselves
ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(colour = class)) +
  geom_smooth(data = filter (mpg, class == "subcompact"), se = FALSE) #we use a filter to select a subset of the data and plot only that subset
# Exercise 
# Line chart = geom_line()
# Boxplot = geom_boxplot()
# Histogram = geom_histogram()
# Area chart = geom_area()
#ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
#  geom_point() + 
#  geom_smooth()
#ggplot() + 
#  geom_point(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
#  geom_smooth(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy))
# Only difference is code structure
#2.22 Transformations and Stats
#2.22.1 Plotting statistics
ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x=cut))
ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  stat_count(mapping = aes(x=cut)) #you can use geom and stats interchangeably
#2.22.2 Overriding defaults in ggplot2
demo <- tribble(
  ~cut,         ~freq,
  "Fair",       1610,
  "Good",       4906,
  "Very Good",  12082,
  "Premium",    13791,
  "Ideal",      21551
)
demo

ggplot(data = demo) +
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = freq), stat = "identity") #
#override teh defautl mappinf 
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = stat(prop), group = 1))
#Warning: `stat(prop)` was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
#2.22.3 Plotting statistical details 
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  stat_summary(
    mapping = aes(x = cut, y = depth),
    fun.min = min,
    fun.max = max,
    fun = median)
#2.23 Aesthetic adjestments 
#use aesthetic colour\fill to change aspects of bar colours
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, colour = cut))
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = cut))
#new variable clarity
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity))
#Position adjestmetns ( identity (raw data), fill (changes heights) and dodge (which forces #ggplot2 to not put things on top of each other))
#To alter transparency (alpha)
ggplot(data = diamonds, mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity)) + 
  geom_bar(alpha = 1/5, position = "identity")
#To color the bar outlines with no fill color
ggplot(data = diamonds, mapping = aes(x = cut, colour = clarity)) + geom_bar(fill = NA, position = "identity")
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity), position = "fill")
ggplot(data = diamonds) + 
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = cut, fill = clarity), position = "dodge")
ggplot(data = mpg) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = displ, y = hwy), position = "jitter")
#2.24 The layered grammar of graphics 
#ggplot(data = <DATA>) + 
#  <GEOM_FUNCTION>(
#     mapping = aes(<MAPPINGS>),
#     stat = <STAT>, 
#     position = <POSITION>
#  ) +
#  <FACET_FUNCTION>
```

library(ggplot2)

#4.5 Conditional Logic - filtering your data
##uses round brackets () for the logical condition
###curly braces {} for the action if that condition is true
#Tidyverse Alternative: Vectorised Conditionals (dplyr)
###The if_else(condition, true_output, false_output) function evaluates an entire column item-by-item

####Load tidyverse (if not already loaded)
library(tidyverse)

# Sample coral data
coral_monitoring <- tibble(
  site = c("Site_A", "Site_B", "Site_C"),
  depth_m = c(12, 35, 8)
)

# Classify depth using if_else
coral_monitoring <- coral_monitoring %>% 
  mutate(zone = if_else(depth_m > 30, "Deep Reef", "Shallow Reef"))

#Task: 

## What do you think that function mutate() does?

###The mutate() function is used to add new variables or transform existing variables in a data frame. ###It allows you to create new columns based on the values of other columns. To learn more ?mutate

##How can we get more information about it? What about the %>% symbol?
###The %>% symbol, also known as the "pipe" operator, passes the output of one function as the first argument to the next function. It helps make code more readable and easier to understand by allowing you to chain multiple operations together in a sequential manner, flowing from left to right. To learn more ?`%>%`

#case_when()
#more than two possibilities, stacking multiple if-else blocks becomes unreadable. case_when() provides a clean, sequential evaluation layout using formula tildes (~)

coral_monitoring <- coral_monitoring %>% 
  mutate(reef_category = case_when(
    depth_m < 10  ~ "Lagoon / Flats",
    depth_m <= 30 ~ "Crest / Slope",
    depth_m > 30  ~ "Mesophotic / Deep",
    TRUE          ~ "Unclassified" # Catch-all remainder
  ))

#Task: Environmental Stress Classification
library(dplyr) # For tibble, mutate, case_when

marine_stations <- tibble(
  salinity = c(35, 28, 32, 12)
) %>%
  mutate(
    environment_type = case_when(
      salinity < 15 ~ "Estuarine",
      salinity >= 15 & salinity <= 30 ~ "Brackish",
      salinity > 30 ~ "Marine"
    )
  )

marine_stations

# 4.6 Automation — Iterating Efficiently
##Base R: for-loops
### Classic loop anatomy
for (year in 2020:2024) {
  print(paste("Processing climate data for year:", year))
}
### Loop across index sequences
transect_lengths <- c(50, 100, 25, 75)

for (i in seq_along(transect_lengths)) {
  print(paste("Transect number", i, "measures", transect_lengths[i], "metres."))
}
#Tidyverse Alternative: Functional Programming (purrr)
#Other functions
###map() Returns a flexible List structure
###map_dbl() Returns a vector of Decimals / Numeric values
###map_chr() Returns a vector of Text strings / Characters
###map_df() Returns a combined Data Frame / Tibble

##Comparison Example: Calculating Square Roots of Site Vectors
###Using a standard for-loop:
site_areas <- c(144, 400, 625)
results <- numeric(length(site_areas)) # Must build an empty container first

for(i in seq_along(site_areas))
  results[i] <- sqrt(site_areas[i])

###Using the purrr equivalent:
library(purrr)
####Map directly and define your expected output type explicitly
mapped_results <- map_dbl(site_areas, sqrt)

###Iterating Across Complex Groups
####Iterate a summary function over split lists of data
iris %>% 
  split(.$Species) %>% 
  map(~summary(.x))

##Task using chattr: 
library(purrr) # For map_dbl

# Sample list of fish count data
fish_counts_list <- list(
  reef_a = c(10, 12, 8, 15, 11),
  reef_b = c(20, 18, 22, 19, 25),
  reef_c = c(5, 7, 6, 9, 8)
)

# Using a for-loop
mean_counts_for_loop <- vector("double", length(fish_counts_list))
for (i in seq_along(fish_counts_list)) {
  mean_counts_for_loop[i] <- mean(fish_counts_list[[i]])
}

# Using purrr::map_dbl
mean_counts_purrr <- map_dbl(fish_counts_list, mean)

# Display results
cat("Mean counts (for-loop):\n")
print(mean_counts_for_loop)
cat("\nMean counts (purrr::map_dbl):\n")
print(mean_counts_purrr)
